slides.texte_overlay:
5 body habits that drain
your presence in a crowd
Habit 1: standing at the edge of the room. Hugging the wall makes you look like you want to disappear. Step a few metres in, closer to where people actually talk.
Habit 2: hiding behind your drink. Taking a sip every time there's a pause looks nervous. Hold it low, and let a short silence be just that, a pause.
Habit 3: tense, raised shoulders. Stress pulls them up toward your ears. Take a breath and drop them down. Relaxed shoulders change your whole silhouette.
Habit 4: talking to the floor. When you're unsure, your eyes drop. Look at faces instead, even briefly. Eye contact makes your words land with more weight.
Habit 5: moving too much. Swaying, fidgeting, shifting from foot to foot. Stillness looks calm, and calm is the core of real presence. Plant your feet and let your body rest.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. A busy, curious mind relaxes the body, and you'll stand taller in any crowd you walk into.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. A curious mind relaxes the body in any crowd.

slides.texte_overlay: The fix: pick one habit per event. Notice it once, correct it, enjoy the rest of the evening. Small fixes, repeated, build a strong presence over a few weeks.
